checks_run: case_id set and order match cases.json
turn_index lists are 1-based and match cases.json per case
field set and order match the rubric schema exactly
route values are drawn from the five rubric routes
responsibility, tone and overall are Green, Yellow, Red, Gray or null
null ratings on Intake, Scope and Message-template mode; non-null on rated routes
overall equals the Red > Gray > Yellow > Green derivation from responsibility and tone
at most three required question topics per turn
every required question topic appears in the allowed question list
every required revision fact appears in the allowed revision list
topic, fact and invariant lists are sorted and duplicate free
critical invariants use only the eight canonical tokens and are never empty
no required revision facts on turns rated Green overall
every turn carries a non-empty rationale

interpretation_notes: Recipient context: recipient_description was treated as scenario context available to the reviewer alongside the turn text, since several cases are only ratable with it and BH-017 turn three restates it consistently rather than contradicting it.

Ground truth: case_designer_notes were treated as the true state of the world for deciding whether an omission or claim in a draft is materially wrong, while question topics and placeholders capture what a reviewer who cannot see those notes must ask for rather than assert.
Gray was reserved for turns where the governing content is genuinely unrecoverable (BH-027 glare, BH-028 crop, BH-030 occluded owner column) rather than used for any case with an unstated detail.

BH-029 is Red rather than Gray because the legible refunds tile (zero, queue not yet opened) directly contradicts the sender's stated intent; the unreadable headline count is handled separately as a placeholder.
Question and fact tokens are canonical shorthand, not required wording; the allowed lists are intended to admit any semantically equivalent phrasing of the same topic or fact.
limitations: Single-labeler judgement produced without discussion; boundary calls between Yellow and Red on the responsibility cases (BH-007, BH-009) and between tone Yellow and Red (BH-012, BH-015, BH-016) are the most likely points of honest disagreement with a second labeler.

Route assignment for BH-026 (Intake rather than a rated Normal review) and for the four image cases (rated Normal with Gray rather than Intake) reflects a reading of the rubric alone, since no specification, plan or scorer was consulted.

Allowed lists are best-effort enumerations of semantically acceptable topics and facts; they may omit acceptable variants that a reviewer could reasonably raise, so an output token outside a list should be re-read against the rubric before being scored as unnecessary or unsupported.

For the six green control cases and BH-018 turn two the allowed question lists are deliberately empty, encoding the judgement that no question on those turns can change route, rating or a safe revision.
Image reading was done from the frozen PNGs as rendered; no enhancement, upscaling or OCR tooling was applied, and no attempt was made to recover glare-saturated, cropped or occluded regions.
No cross-checking against any other labeler, Skill output, or historical label was possible or attempted by design.
